title: Monolithic 3D FPGA Design and Synthesis with Back-End-of-Line Configuration Memories
problem: Conventional FPGAs use bulky Si SRAM for configuration, occupying area and increasing reconfigurable circuit overhead; this limits routing efficiency and increases latency for densely integrated FPGA designs.
motivation: Post-Moore era demands area-efficient FPGA designs; monolithic 3D integration with novel materials can achieve better area-time-power trade-offs by reducing configuration memory footprint.
method: The design stacks special transistors—amorphous oxide semiconductors (AOS) made from materials like W-doped indium oxide and tin oxide—in the back-end-of-line (BEOL) layers above the main logic blocks (CLBs). These AOS transistors store configuration data with less power leakage than conventional silicon SRAM, shrinking the space needed. By placing the FPGA's switch and connection blocks directly above the logic blocks using AOS pass gates (transistors that act as controllable switches), routing distances shrink, reducing interconnect latency.
key_novelty: This design replaces silicon SRAM configuration memory with amorphous oxide semiconductor transistors (AOS—materials like W-doped indium oxide and tin oxide) stacked in the upper layers of the chip, positioning configuration storage close to the logic blocks and reducing routing latency.
contributions: AOS transistor-based configuration memory design for BEOL integration
Monolithic 3D FPGA architecture leveraging BEOL transistors
Physics-based TCAD modeling of AOS devices for robust circuit design
3.4x lower AT² product, 27% lower latency, 26% lower routing power on LLM/hyperdimensional benchmarks
limitations: Not discussed; AOS technology is still in development.
primary_theme: Monolithic 3D FPGA using BEOL AOS transistors for configuration memory
